analysis.title: Xcel Energy Inc. (XEL): Raising capex and growth outlook; see peer leading 10% EPS CAGR through 2031; Buy
key_insights: GS reiterates Buy on Xcel Energy (XEL) after 3Q26 results and raises the 12-month price target to $95 from $93. The stock was $79.82, implying 19.0% upside and 22% total return.

XEL introduced a $70bn 2027-31 capital plan. It supports about 11% rate base growth through 2031, taking rate base from about $68bn in 2026 to about $112bn in 2031. SPS is the biggest driver at about 21% rate base growth.
Management expects 10%+ average EPS growth from 2027-30, off the midpoint of 2026 guidance, then 9%+ average growth through 2031. GS calls this among the strongest growth outlooks in its coverage.

The base plan excludes the investment needed to serve another 4 GW of data center demand XEL targets through year-end 2027. XEL sees $10bn+ of additional investment opportunities from data centers, generation RFPs and transmission, including 15+ GW of additional generation needs.

GS embeds about $79bn of 2027-31 capex, about $9bn above the $70bn base plan, and sees risk as still skewed to the upside versus its new capex outlook. Estimated incremental capex from NSP, PSCo and SPS generation projects is about $8.7bn through 2031.
Every additional $1bn of capex adds 15-20 bps to rate base growth, versus 20-25 bps previously. The lower sensitivity reflects the larger rate base.

XEL has about 2 GW of data centers contracted or under construction. It expects to sign about 1 GW more by year-end 2026 and about 3 GW by 2027. The strongest near-term opportunities are the Upper Midwest and SPS, and Colorado is likely later because of its large load tariff.
XEL estimates $6-8bn of investment per 1 GW of data center demand, including third-party generation. It has more than 20 GW of potential additional data center demand in its pipeline.

The new capital plan requires about $8bn of equity and about $26bn of additional debt, with about 40% of the equity already contracted. The company expects FFO/debt of about 18% by 2031. The equity need could be lower for projects added in 2030-31.

GS EPS estimates for 2026-30 are $4.16/$4.57/$5.05/$5.59/$6.20, versus $4.16/$4.56/$5.03/$5.51/$6.12 previously. It introduces a 2031 EPS estimate of $6.77. This implies a 10% EPS CAGR from 2026-31, above management's 9%+ outlook.

The price target applies a 19.5x multiple to Q5-Q8 earnings, unchanged. This is a 3x premium to GS's baseline multiple for leverage to renewables and transmission, above-average growth versus peers and execution track record.
GS discloses it is a manager or co-manager of a pending underwriting for XEL and has received investment banking compensation from XEL in the past 12 months.

market_movers.rationale: The $70bn 2027-31 capital plan supports about 11% rate base growth and 9%+ EPS growth. GS sees upside from data center and generation RFP capex outside the plan. Price target raised from $93.

sector_views.rationale: GS sees XEL's growth outlook as among the strongest in its coverage, driven by capex, data center demand and transmission. This is a single-stock view and not a stated sector call.

earnings_insights: XEL 3Q26 results were reported before this note, and the note's main update was the new $70bn 2027-31 capital plan. GS gives no 3Q26 EPS or revenue figures in the text.

GS diluted EPS estimates (pre-exceptionals, GS estimates, not reported): 2026E $4.16, 2027E $4.57 (old $4.56), 2028E $5.05 (old $5.03). 2025 actual diluted EPS was $3.80. Quarterly estimates: 4Q26E $0.80, 1Q27E $1.08, 2Q27E $0.81.
Management guidance: 10%+ average EPS growth from 2027-30 off the 2026 guidance midpoint, then 9%+ average growth through 2031.
risk_factors: Failure to close the gap between earned and authorized ROE.
Regulatory clarity: 2031 capex is likely lower due to lack of regulatory clarity that far out.
Funding: free cash flow is negative in every forecast year, and net debt/EBITDA is 5.0-5.6x in the forecast.
